newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: BMW S.AFRICA TO LURE 1 BLN INVESTMENT - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: BMW S.AFRICA TO LURE 1 BLN INVESTMENT - PAPER.

text.p: South African-based German motor firm, BMW South Africa, will attract an additional one billion rand in foreign investment spin-offs into the country from plans to maufacture a new model here for export to world markets, Business Day newspaper said on Tuesday.

BMW spokesman, Deon Ebersohn, told the paper that the planned investment by BMW SA, to enable it to export up to 25,000 new 3-series vehicles a year, was well under way and construction of a new 200 million rand paint shop had begun.
The shop, the first signs of the investment plans, was expected to be commissioned around April next year.

Ebersohn said a number of overseas component suppliers, mostly manufacturers based in Germany that supply parent company Bayerische Motoren-Werke AG, had indicated that they wished to invest in a new plant in South Africa to supply parts for the new range.
The first new 3-series vehicle is expected to roll off BMW SA's production line in the fourth quarter of next year, Business Day said.

Added to the paint shop, a separate export centre to enable the transport to the coast of up to 200 vehicles a day and tooling for the new model, which could cost up to 500 million rand, would be set up.
Production at BMW SA would rise to around 250 vehicles a day from between 80 and 90 currently, the newspaper said.
